sources.title: Ministry aims to transform country into sport and culture hub (Daily News, Botswana Press Agency, 17 Mar 2026: the Minister of Sport and Arts presenting the 2026/27 budget)
sources.said: Upon its enactment, he said government would establish the National Film Commission to foster a local filming culture.

figures.finding: Botswana has no film fund; the Ministry of Sport and Arts commissions films and earmarked P23 million for 2026/27 to buy content (producer-BW.json), the nearest thing to item 4. Not attempted today. Botswana has no production incentive for film or television in force: the minister’s 2026/27 budget speech puts the Cinematography Act before Parliament and a film commission only after it passes (producer-BW.json holds the same). Absence stands on the minister’s statement, not on a text of the law read whole.

sources.said: Upon its enactment, he said government would establish the National Film Commission to foster a local filming culture.

He further said the ministry planned to expand NowTV by relaunching it on the Digital Terrestrial Transmission (DTT) and satellite platforms through local and regional carriers. The minister said P23 million had been earmarked for acquisition of content from 34 producers.

figures.finding: Botswana has no film fund; the Ministry of Sport and Arts commissions films and earmarked P23 million for 2026/27 to buy content (producer-BW.json), the nearest thing to item 4. Not attempted today. The state channel buys content from local producers: P23m for 34 producers in 2026/27 (about P676,000 each on average, arithmetic, not stated). No tariff per episode or hour, and no count of independent series picked up, was found.
